To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the multiple electromagnetic excitation of a nucleus with a fast projectile (heavy ion) is studied theoretically.

the excitation cross section for multiple electromagnetic excitation is proportional to the number of equivalent photons and to the square of the matrix element of the dipole moment between the initial and the final state, which is proportional to the square of B(E1) value.
multiple electromagnetic excitation can be used to probe nuclear structure in a novel way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
electromagnetic excitation of nuclei in relativistic heavy ions collisions, in particular the excitation of low lying rotational states and the coupling to giant dipole vibrations.
the study of the multiple electromagnetic excitation of nuclear states with relativistic heavy ion projectiles.
the study of the excitation of nuclear rotational states with relativistic heavy ion beams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple electromagnetic excitation of nuclei by relativistic heavy ions is a very promising tool for nuclear structure studies.
the multiple electromagnetic excitation of giant dipole resonances is a new and promising method of investigating nuclear structure, especially in the region of high spin states.

the electromagnetic excitation with high energy photons in relativistic ion collisions is an important new tool in nuclear structure studies, complementary to electron scattering and nuclear Raman scattering, and with new possibilities not accessible to these methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the giant dipole resonance can be excited with relativistic heavy ion projectiles with high efficiency and with a very large number of equivalent photons.
we are now able to describe the multiple electromagnetic excitation in a relativistic way.
multiple electromagnetic excitation of giant dipole vibrations with relativistic heavy ion beams opens up a new field of nuclear structure studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the multiple electromagnetic excitation of rotational levels coupled to the giant (dipolar) mode can be used for studying the Brink-hypothesis and also for investigating the structure of rotational levels.
the multiple electromagnetic excitation of rotational nuclei with relativistic heavy ion projectiles is a new tool to study the structure of rotational nuclei.

the multiple electromagnetic excitation of rotational bands with relativistic heavy ion projectiles can be used as a new tool in the investigation of the Brink-hypothesis and in the study of nuclear structure in general.
